sourceEvidence.metricType: external source image metrics (whole_static, facade_band, road_band)

reviewProtocol: Shared regional route/lateral plan, mapped through each model's saved proper camera-center similarity and world matrix. No independent novel-view ground truth; alignment residuals retained.

observations.observation: 0–5.88s: houses and street direction remain readable, but near trees and driveway regions are unstable.
7.25–9.88s: porch railings, the large tree and house edges change shape or smear across views.
2.00s: recognizable windows/roofs; 4.00s and 8.50s: porch and fine foliage remain blurred.
4.00s: several prominent dark wedges cross the road/driveway; lateral tree and porch ghosts also remain.
The sampled residential stretch connects, but near-road holes and occlusion artifacts prevent clean continuity.

comparisons: Same regional route/lateral review plan as the other residential diagnostics, mapped through each saved alignment. The surviving porch/tree smears matter more than tiny source-view metric changes.
These 5,000-step local patches do not establish full-block performance. Preparation, solving and human review are excluded from the short training times.
More pronounced multiple road wedges at 4.00s justify the lower artifact score here. This single reviewed run does not prove priors always hurt.
limits: AI-assisted editorial assessment of eight labelled samples per model, with links to the complete 80-sample review and existing native evidence. Not an independent human panel.
No real-time FPS, fine temporal flicker, physical-phone thermal test, surveyed scale or independent novel-view truth measured.
Human effort and end-to-end elapsed time unknown; source-view metrics are not lateral geometric accuracy.
Different captures, routes, training budgets and encodings make cross-group ranking a provisional asset-utility judgment, not an algorithm leaderboard.
